The Reprise of the True Spear Hero (Web Novel)

This is a continuation from the final episode of *The Spear Hero’s Second Chance*. It’s the “True Tutorial” arc.
“Father! Big Sister! Filo-oooooo! Wait for meeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!”
I barely managed to catch up to Father’s cart as it raced away. But after glancing at me with a face like he’d just swallowed a bitter pill, he turned his gaze forward with a tense expression.
“Filo! Run faster!”
“G-Guaaaaaaaah!”
Filo-tan showed some real grit at Father’s request! This is it! She’s actually enjoying this game of tag with me! Woaaaaah, I won’t lose!
Just as I was thinking that and showing off my leg strength to Filo-tan and my Father, the cart jolted, and the figure sitting on the back looked like it was about to tumble off. Oh, that’s my sister! Isn’t that a little dangerous?
“Raphtalia! Are you okay!?”
“U… uh…”
She looked completely drained and was about to fall off at any moment. She seems to be in pretty bad shape.
“Here we go!”
I gave her a gentle shove to get her back onto the cart, then hopped on myself.
“I caught up to you! I win this game of tag!”
“Tch… He’s not even out of breath.”
And so, my father pulled on the reins and stopped Filo-chan. Then, while holding his shield in a defensive stance, he kept glancing over at my sister. What kind of reaction is this, I wonder?
“What’s the matter?”
“Send Raphtalia over here.”
“Yes, sir. She doesn’t look well.”
Following Father’s instructions, I handed my sister over to him. Seeing my attitude, my Father furrowed his brow and tilted his head.
“Would you like me to cast an anti-nausea spell or a Recovery spell?”

Poison? Why on earth would I need to make my Older Sister drink poison? If anyone’s going to drink it, it should be the Crimson Swine. I’d like to make him drink a poison that makes him writhe in agony, just like what he did to Fleon-chan. Well, he’s already out of this world, though. HAHAHA.

Let me think about it. …No matter how I look at it, I can’t think of anyone but Crimson Swine!

“No! It’s your fault for killing him!”

Oh, he’s even more hostile than the Father in my memories. In my hazy memories, my Father used to sigh a lot when talking to me and always seemed gloomy. However, it’s the greatest honor to be able to sense what’s really on his mind. I’ll keep this up and prove myself to be his right-hand man!

As he said that, my Father looked at me with concern. This Motoyasu—tears of emotion are welling up in my eyes. Unlike in the previous loop, you still have a kind heart that wants to be closer to the Father from the first world! That’s exactly the kind of Father you are. I’ll follow you wherever you go!

Oh? Filo-chan seems concerned about us and is looking this way, glancing around. Leave it to me, Filo-chan. I’ll definitely show you the path to glory alongside my Father… the Filolial Road.

My sister, who had been slumped over, opened her eyes and turned toward Father. Then, realizing I was there, she staggered and tried to stand up hurriedly. Her expression was pained, but it was also clearly on guard. Hmm… Why am I being treated with such suspicion?

The older sister looked at me with a shocked expression. So, I gave a firm nod. It’s an undeniable fact, after all. The Crimson Swine is a being unworthy of living in this world. In fact, the longer he stays alive, the more vitality is drained from the world.

The surprised Older Sister looked at my Father, and he nodded silently. She’s still staring at me with a look that says she can’t believe it. All right, I should have made it clear by now that I’m on her side. From here on out, I’ll prove that I’m someone she can trust.

My father is running his fingers through his hair. You’ll damage your cuticles if you keep doing that!

My Older Sister is looking at me with furrowed brows. Well, I suppose it’s hard to make her believe me right away. But I’ll keep talking patiently, just like in the previous loop. Because I believe that’s the true path to peace.

Oh? Father’s reaction… Ah, come to think of it, he doesn’t know the real reason why he’s been framed. In that case, I suppose I’d best start by explaining that.
“Um, what do you mean by ‘Father’?”
“Because you’re Filo-chan’s Father, of course.”

It seems my sister is also starting to recover from her motion sickness.
“So, Father, don’t you want to know why you were falsely accused of rape?”
At my question, Father glared at me intensely while clenching his fists. Then, as if choosing his words carefully, he said:
“…What do you know? What are you trying to say with that mocking attitude?”
“It’s the truth I learned from the future. Of course, the things I did without realizing it are facts that can’t be changed, but I’m truly remorseful.”

Just as I expected from my Father. You really do know me well. My sister seems convinced, too. It’s true—the me before I recalled my memories of the future would never have killed Crimson Swine. I’ll use this as a breakthrough to gain their trust!

He’s quick to assess the situation. I’d like to learn from that.
“Then I’ll tell you. This country, Melromarc, has a state religion that regards the Shield Hero as the enemy.”

You seem troubled. I suppose there’s nothing to be done about it.

*The Rise of the Shield Hero*. A work that began as a serialization on the “Let’s Become Novelists” website, was later published in book form, and even adapted into an anime.
It’s the story of Naofumi Iwatani, a college student who came to the library to read, and who, while reading a book titled *The Book of the Four Holy Weapons* that he happened to find, is summoned to another world as the Shield Hero—the hero who saves the world depicted within the book. From this clichéd beginning, he becomes entangled in various conspiracies.
Starting with the other three Heroes—who can’t seem to shake their “video game” mentality—the story follows Naofumi as he fends off conspiracies and false accusations orchestrated by Melromarc, the summoning nation that seeks to persecute him because, from a religious perspective, he is the Shield Hero of an enemy nation. I’ve been reading this series since I was in high school. It’s a work that divides readers—some see it as unconventional yet classic, while others view it as classic yet unconventional—and many find it stressful to read.
After *The Rise of the Shield Hero* concluded, the author wrote a new side story titled *The Spear Hero’s Redo*. This story begins with the Spear Hero—who was portrayed as the main antagonist in *The Rise of the Shield Hero*—getting trapped in a loop in a parallel world. Even though he knows the future, the clumsy Spear Hero—whose personality has changed—tries his best to achieve his ideal future… well, not exactly.
It’s a story about him being infatuated with Filo, one of the heroines from *The Rising of the Shield Hero*, while regretting his past mistakes, struggling to help the Shield Hero, and doing his best to meet Filo. I remember this well because I used to read and enjoy both of these stories a lot. I pored over the characters depicted in the novel’s illustrations and across various media. That’s exactly why there’s no way I could mistake her.

Since I’ve never seen any other Filolial-samas fly besides Filo-tan, there’s no mistake about it. Well then… a trivial conversation with the Crimson Swine… no, perhaps it would be best to go kill them right now.
“Fleon-chan. I’d like you to wait here for a bit.”
“Kue!”
After asking Fleon-chan to mind the place, I returned to Melromarc Castle via the portal.
I’ve arrived at Melromarc Castle. Shall I slaughter the Crimson Swine before high tide? I’m thinking about how to deal with them so there are no loose ends.
It’s a dangerous time—if I make a wrong move, my Father might end up taking the fall for a crime he didn’t commit… I don’t really care about Ren or Itsuki, but as for my Father… ugh, I’d really like to lend a hand to Filo-tan and Big Sister. It’s a huge hassle, you see. If only I knew where the Queen was right now, this would be a piece of cake, but all I can tell is that she’s probably somewhere in the southwest. With these thoughts in mind, I spent about an hour strolling through the castle and its gardens.
“So… I’m telling you to give it back!”
“Shut up! Don’t you get it yet?! If you keep making up excuses and defying me, I’ll have you executed on the spot!”
“But! That’s a Filolial egg—I cherish it more than my own life! Without that child, I…”
Hm? A Filolial egg, you say? I can hear some kind of argument with a guard near the castle gate.
“What’s going on?”
I rush over to where they’re talking and ask what’s going on. The guard salutes me. After all, since I’m a favorite of Crimson Swine and Trash, my standing is pretty high at this stage.
“Ha! This old man is protesting, demanding the return of the Filolial egg that was confiscated!”
“What…? Are you really doing something so terrible? Return it immediately!”
Confiscating a Filolial-sama’s egg… and if you forcibly took it from the owner herself, that’s an unforgivable act of barbarism! A scoundrel like Takt deserves to be made an example of!
“Um… regarding that matter…”
The guard whispers to me, as if trying to avoid the issue.
“I believe the Filolial presented to the Spear Hero on Malty’s orders is the very egg this old man is testifying about.”
“What?!”
Is it because I wanted it?! Ugh… How should I get out of this one? No, there’s no doubt this old man knows a great deal about Fleon-chan. I absolutely must talk to him!
“I understand. Old man, come talk to me for a moment about the Filolial.”
I give the guard a sidelong glance and a signal, as if to say I’ll handle the persuasion, then push the old man’s back and lead him straight out through the castle gate toward the town below.
“Where do you think you’re taking me?! Hurry! Hurry up and give that child back to me…”
Ah, it’s true that I’ll have to explain the situation. I whisper to the old man.
“That egg has already hatched, and I’m currently in possession of it. I’d like you to come with me so I can show you the way. However… we’ll have to travel a bit, but it’s dangerous if we don’t keep this a secret.”
“You say that…”
“It’s flying… Filolial-sama.”
At my words, the old man fell silent. He must have realized I wasn’t lying.
